prompt: Why do old images of space rocket launches look better than newer, digital ones?
response: Old images of space rocket launches often appear better because they were captured using high-quality film, which has a unique aesthetic. The grain and texture of the film can add warmth and depth to the images. In contrast, early digital cameras might have had lower resolution and dynamic range, leading to less impressive images. However, modern digital photography has since improved significantly, capturing launches with clarity and detail.
